text:
The Devils are the real thing, and the numbers have been saying so all season. At 18-8-0 with 36 points they sit at a 97% playoff chance by our simulations, and unlike a lot of fast starters, they've earned it: 57% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) overall, and a points total that matches what their chances produced almost exactly. Friday's 5-3 comeback over Calgary, their third straight win, was typical. They out-chanced the Flames 3.88 to 2.33 and kept pushing until the goals came.

The two top lines are why. Jesper Bratt, Jack Hughes and Arseny Gritsyuk own 61% of the expected goals and a 12-8 goal edge; Timo Meier, Nico Hischier and Luke Evangelista are at 60%. Meier is the story of the month, ten points in his last ten and, per Daily Faceoff, now Switzerland's all-time leading NHL goal-scorer. Brett Pesce and Luke Hughes are 24-12 in goals together.

The worry is the net behind Connor Hellebuyck. Jake Allen is .860 over his last five starts, 5.5 goals worse than expected, and allowed three on 21 shots Friday. Brenden Dillon's four-game suspension thins the blue line. Watch Saturday, when Hellebuyck faces the Jets for the first time since Winnipeg traded him.
